original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Add a charged common-A broadcast-readout call to the five-source universal connector, using the fixed ten-toggle path and all 31 nonzero target masks.
scope_change_reason: The selector card asks for one added connector operation. This run fixes one new operation R_S and changes the output-map hypothesis from arbitrary A_i to one common A, then prices all target writes and routing. It does not extend the source-call alphabet as in current DUO/triple-sum work.
bottleneck_link: The operation can amortize one full common A evaluation across several output rows at a shared connector prefix. Its relevance depends on an actual supplier exposing common A and on the charged target-routing bill being below the saved evaluations.
stop_rule: Stop after the fixed two-source minimal instance and the five-source all-mask witness are checked symbolically and on exact dense F2 instances, with the complete parameterized invoice and three failing controls. Do not search other words or claim supplier admission.
evidence: The exact five-source witness uses 10 B calls, 10 distinct common-A broadcast evaluations, and 64 target-row writes; the same path uses 64 ordinary A evaluations in the original alphabet. The exact break-even is 54*a + D_unicast - D_broadcast. A dense reference replay checks 111 basis columns and 64 arbitrary dirty cases; the two-source fixture checks 18 basis columns and 32 dirty cases. Three omission/corruption controls reject.
author: OpenAI Codex with GPT-6
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex/GPT-6 assistance authored the construction statement, cost model, certificate derivation, verifier and package. No subagents or other model outputs were used.

open_questions.question: Can a selected recursive supplier expose the same exact A evaluation as a streamed result to multiple dirty output rows while keeping D_broadcast - D_unicast below 54*a?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a positive fully priced realization in the selected supplier can turn this local interface construction into a conditional kappa improvement.
open_questions.first_step: Search the selected source manifest for two output roles with a byte-identical A map, then write the exact recursive child and target-update contract for those roles.
open_questions.blocked_by: The selected #1094 construction does not currently identify a common-A broadcast provider or an admitted per-target write tariff.
